title: Ali Qushji, astronomer of Samarkand and Constantinople
summary: Ali Qushji, born in Samarkand in 1403, worked on Ulugh Beg's astronomical tables at the Samarkand observatory until 1449. He then moved through Herat and Tabriz and settled in Constantinople around 1472, where Mehmed II welcomed him; he taught at Ottoman madrasas, including Hagia Sophia, and died there in 1474.

importance.justification: Leading astronomer of the Samarkand school whose commentary on the Zij of Ulugh Beg and teaching texts carried that tradition into Ottoman scholarship.

beats.caption: After Ulugh Beg's assassination in 1449 ended the Samarkand observatory's work, Ali Qushji left for Herat.
Following Sultan Abu Said's defeat by Uzun Hasan in 1469 he relocated to Tabriz.
Around 1472 he settled in Constantinople, taught at the Sahn-i Seman madrasa and headed the Hagia Sophia madrasa, shaping Ottoman learning.
